findings.title: 'Fine-level GMRES' has never been run at production scale and the only data point argues against assuming it converges
findings.detail: The fine-level GMRES change is only a cap increase: GMRES_MAXIT 5 → 40, restart kept at 100, so 4000 iterations. No production 0.125 mm solve was run; the note says so. The only fine-level data point is the founder diagnostic, which stalled at the old 500-iteration cap with solver_tol 1.2e-3. That number is residual-dominated. The repository disagrees with itself on what the fine level needs: the code comment above GMRES_RESTART says ~800-1000 iterations, while the note says ~430. Iteration growth under restarted GMRES(100) is not guaranteed to follow the ×1.8-per-level trend seen at 133 → 238 iterations. The only check at 0.125 mm is test_solver_tol_usable_at_every_refinement, a two-wire plane system. It says nothing about convergence on a 7-8 M-unknown layout system. The claim holds for 0.5 and 0.25 mm. Whether GMRES converges at 0.125 mm, and so the convergence gate itself, is unestablished.
findings.evidence: l2_layout.py lines 1636-1642 (comment: '0.125 mm needs ~800-1000') vs the note 'I expect about 430 iterations at 1e-7'; note: 'The production 0.125 mm solve has not run here'; founder diagnostic: '> 500 (cap 100 × 5)', solver_tol 1.2e-3.
findings.suggested_check: Treat the --vm run's gmres_flags, gmres_iters and solver_tol at refinement 2 as the acceptance test for this item before E002 depends on k*+1.

findings.title: Cost-gate margin at k_star is within the stated run-to-run variation; RSS was measured under memory pressure
findings.detail: The 6-die k_star solve used 2011 CPU-s, 84 % of the 2400 s gate. The note gives ±25 % variation with machine load, and 2011 × 1.25 ≈ 2514 > 2400, so a DoD re-run can fail without any code change. The RSS figures were taken with 8.8 GB of swap in use. The author's own control shows they read low under that condition: the 0.5 mm child gave 2.28 GB in the run and 3.58 GB standalone. My own rough memory estimate puts the k* 6-die solve at ~8-10 GB, which agrees with 8.9-9.3 GB. That estimate counts the Krylov basis (101 × ~2.1 M × 16 B ≈ 3.4 GB), the half-spectrum plane tables (2 × 154k × 22² × 8 B ≈ 1.2 GB), the 82.8 M near pairs as CSR K plus Cx (≈ 2 GB), and the pFFT stencils (≈ 0.8 GB). So the 12 GB gate is probably met, but no clean measurement shows it.
findings.evidence: cost.json: cpu_s 2011.46, peak_rss_gb 8.918; note: 'This run had 8.8 GB of swap in use', '2.28 GB in the quick run … 3.58 GB' standalone; parent time 2553 s user + 801 s sys equals the sum of the children's cpu_s (3353 s), so ~24 % was system time.
findings.suggested_check: Re-run the 6-die k* child alone on an idle machine and record cpu_user_s, cpu_sys_s and peak RSS (or phys_footprint).

findings.title: The k*+1 cost extrapolation does not apply the note's own scaling factors
findings.detail: The note says it applies 'the same factors per stage'. Its GMRES factor is ×11.7 (500.87/42.93), which gives 501 × 11.7 ≈ 5860 s. The note writes ~4700 s. The grid stage at ×7.6 gives ≈ 2140 s, not ~2250 s. Recomputed, the 2-die k*+1 solve is ≈ 2140 + 254 + 5860 ≈ 8250 s wall, or ≈ 10,350 CPU-s at the measured CPU/wall ratio of 1.255. That is ≈ 2.9 CPU-h, not 2.5, and 6 dies would be ≈ 3.4 CPU-h. With 3.4 CPU-h per refinement layout, the 60 CPU-h envelope allows m ≈ 9 at n = 60, not 11. The table is optimistic by ~15-20 % on m.
findings.evidence: stage_s at refinement 0 and 1: gmres 42.93 → 500.87 s, grid 36.87 → 280.70 s; note: 'GMRES ~4700 s (~430 iterations) … ~9000 CPU-s ≈ 2.5 CPU-h'.
findings.suggested_check: Recompute the planning table with the per-stage factors stated in the note, or replace it with the --vm measurement.

findings.title: The absolute lateral discretization error at k_star is not stated and is probably larger than the 1 % step gate suggests
findings.detail: I checked the diagnostic's ratios: steps −0.958 % and −0.589 %, contraction 0.615, order 0.70. Applying that geometric contraction to the measured k*−1 → k* steps gives a remaining error at k* of about step×0.61/(1−0.61). That is ≈ −1.2 % for seed 7 and ≈ −1.9 % for seed 11. In other words, L(k*) sits ~1.2-1.9 % above the lateral limit, and the offset differs by family (~0.7 points). The gate only bounds the next step (< 1 %), not this bias. If E002 compares L2 with L1 or L3 on absolute values, this layout-dependent offset is a systematic error that the note never states.
findings.suggested_check: Once the --vm run gives three levels per layout, report a Richardson-extrapolated L∞ and the k* bias for each layout.

findings.title: Skin-resolution check covers top Cu only; backside Cu misses the 2 % criterion, and --quick exits 0 on empty gates
findings.detail: skin_resolution sets resolved from top_cu zs_rel_err ≤ ZS_TOL (2 %) only. Backside Cu's 1-D Z_s error is 8.3 %, so the docstring's 'thickness layers … resolve the 20 MHz skin depth at every level' does not hold for that slab under the stated test. Its second layer is 20.4 µm (1.4 δ), and the note's 'graded the same way' hides a grading ratio of 6.2 against 2.25 for top Cu. The impact on L is bounded by the +2-layer sensitivity: −0.043 %, measured in attempt 4, not in this DoD run. Separately, in --quick mode convergence and sensitivity are empty lists. all([]) is True, so the script returns 0, and the exit code does not show that those gates were not evaluated.
findings.evidence: cost.json skin_resolution.backside_cu.zs_rel_err = 0.0832, layers_um 3.30 / 20.43 / 126.27; benchmark main(): ok = … all(c['converged'] for c in res['convergence']) …
findings.suggested_check: Record backside resolution against its own stated tolerance, and make --quick report the convergence and sensitivity gates as 'not evaluated' rather than passing.

findings.title: Snapping changes the layout population for every seed and makes the parameter space much coarser
findings.detail: Each draw is unchanged, but values are now rounded to 0.5 mm: s ∈ {4.0, 4.5, 5.0, 5.5} with probabilities 1/6, 1/3, 1/3, 1/6; g, dg ∈ {1.5, 2.0, 2.5}; e ∈ {0, 0.5, …}; xs snapped. Every seed therefore yields different layouts than before this change. A different DRC outcome can also shift the reject-and-resample stream. Any earlier results keyed to generate_layouts(seed) are not comparable, and the population is less diverse, which matters for E002's ranking statistics. This is in scope (a 'snapped generator' is claimed), but downstream consumers should know.
findings.suggested_check: Confirm that no registered spec or existing result depends on layouts from the pre-snap generator.

independent_checks_performed: I could not run anything: Bash was denied in this session, so I did not execute the DoD benchmark, pytest or ruff. Every check below was done by reading code and recomputing by hand.

Generator alignment for every seed, worked through halfbridge._rows and _build symbolically. All housing constants (Y_BOT 1.5, pads, X_ROW_L 9, X_PH_R 61, X_EDGE 68, the 7.0 mm PHASE column, margins 1/3/4) are multiples of 0.5 mm. Every trace edge is a sum of these and the snapped s, g, dg, e, and every max() picks between on-grid values. Die footprints are xs + i(s+dg) .. +s and y0 .. y0+s with y0 on the grid. xs = snap(·) stays within [10, 60−ld] because both bounds are on the grid. So every layout is on the 0.5 mm grid, and therefore on the 0.25 and 0.125 mm lattices, which start at −8 mm. This does not depend on seed sampling.

Checked the lattice and refusal code (layout_lattice, cell_fill, _snap_aligned, check_on_lattice). Whole-cell extent check, ALIGN_TOL on fractions, two-net refusal and the exact per-net area accounting are consistent with the claim. With aligned footprints, the die-short mask built from cell centres is exact.

Re-derived slab_surface_impedance from the 1-D diffusion equation, H = H0 sinh(k(t−z))/sinh(kt), giving Z = (k/σ)coth(kt). Checked its low-frequency limit 1/(σt) + jωμ0t/3. Re-derived the three layer-average flux kernels in layered_surface_impedance: t_j(e_i+e_{i+1})/2, t_j(e_j+t_j/2), t_j(e_j+t_j/3). All match the code.

Checked the layer grading numbers: δ(20 MHz, σ = 5.8e7) = 14.78 µm, which matches cost.json. δ(100 MHz)/2 = 3.304 µm, which equals the first layer. The top-Cu half-stack sums to 150.0 µm with a constant ratio of 2.251. The backside half-stack sums to 150.0 µm with ratio ≈ 6.18. Filament counts: 1 + 4×6 = 25 and 1 + 5×6 = 31, matching filaments_per_wire and the finer variant.

Recomputed every DoD-relevant number in the attempt-5 cost.json against the note's tables: L, R, CPU-s, RSS, iterations, solver_tol, unknowns. All 12 entries agree. The step rel_change, (11.029203 − 11.114978)/11.029203 = −0.007777, and R_rel_change −0.00205 match. The cost.json content satisfies the DoD assertions: k_star = 1, die counts {2, 6} at k*, a k*−1 solve present, L inside 1e-9..1e-7 H, cpu_s and RSS at k* under the gates, solver_tol < 1e-3.

Re-derived the a-posteriori residual bound's premise. For M = R + jωL with R diagonal and positive and L real symmetric, Re(x*Mx) = x*Rx ≥ r_min‖x‖², so σ_min(M) ≥ r_min and |rᵀM⁻¹r| ≤ ‖r‖²/r_min. This supports loosening GMRES_TOL from 1e-9 to 1e-7 without loosening the stated solver_tol.

Analysed whether point contacts are a source of non-convergence. Radial sheet current from a point gives B ~ μ0I/(4πρ) only within |z| ≲ ρ, so the local field energy integral is finite (∝ r) and the log term is cut off by the plate spacing, not the cell size. No log divergence of L under lateral refinement is expected from the bilinear port or foot contacts.

Recomputed the diagnostic's contraction (0.615) and order (0.70), the note's k*→k*+1 extrapolations (−0.47 %, −0.73 %), the per-die cost fit (212 CPU-s per die, mean 0.44 CPU-h), the E002 budget table and the k*+1 per-stage extrapolation. The last of these is inconsistent; see findings.

Made a rough analytic memory estimate at k* (Krylov basis, plane-table half spectra, near-pair sparse storage, pFFT stencils): ≈ 8-10 GB, consistent with the measured 8.9-9.3 GB and under the 12 GB gate.
Checked physical plausibility: L = 8-13 nH for a 70×40 mm DBC half-bridge is a normal range, interleaved < u_shaped is the expected ordering, and 6 dies < 2 dies is the expected direction.
caveats: Valid only for the 0.5 and 0.25 mm levels. The 0.125 mm production solve, its GMRES convergence under the new 4000-iteration cap, the k*→k*+1 convergence gate and the wire-filament sensitivity on this ladder are all unmeasured and deferred to the --vm run.

The cost-gate pass at k_star was measured on one 16 GB laptop under memory pressure, with an 84 % CPU margin for 6 dies against a stated ±25 % variation. A DoD re-run can fail on CPU, and the RSS values are probably low.
The k_star choice limits only the next lateral step to < 1 %. The extrapolated absolute lateral bias of L at k* is ~1.2-1.9 % and depends on the layout.
